::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jany 23d 1865  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Mrs Clare Roels
:::

My dear [Christabel,](people/person_329.qmd)
Here is the first Golden egg that a Gosling has yet laid, though I am afraid it is only a paper one! Many thanks to you for the Eagle that contributed to it[^1]. You know that I have got a new [Gosling](organizations/other_104.qmd)- [Elizabeth Catharine Yonge](people/person_1603.qmd), Eton - to the brood the Cobra di Capello- (because she wears spectacles)[^2] She is only 15, but will be a capital one in time. She is staying here now, so your Sidney questions will be the first she will see. I hope to take her up to be introduced to [Kittiwake](people/person_887.qmd)- Have you got the [Barnacle](organizations/other_89.qmd) yet?

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: ‘The Eagle of one house is the Goose of Another'. She had evidently contributed to *MP*, and the 'golden egg' enclosed with the letter was a cheque to Coleridge for £5 which was cashed on 17 February. The story had appeared in December 1864 and was later reprinted in Coleridge's *The Face of Carlyon and Other Stories* (1875).
[^2]: The gosling, Elizabeth Catherine Yonge (1847/8-1905). In fact she called herself Cricket. Census returns suggest that she was born in 1847/8 so she may have been older than CMY thought.
